statement: You are given an undirected graph: a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1) and a list of edges [u, v].

An edge is a bridge (a critical connection) when deleting it leaves some pair of vertices that used to be connected with no path between them. An edge that lies on a cycle is never a bridge, because the rest of the cycle still joins its endpoints.
Return all bridges, in any order, or none if there are no bridges.

examples.explanation: Vertices 0, 1 and 2 form a triangle, so none of its edges is a bridge. The edges 0 − 3 and 3 − 4 are the only links to 3 and 4, so deleting either one cuts part of the graph off.
Every edge lies on the cycle 0 − 1 − 2 − 3 − 0, so no single deletion disconnects the graph.
